accepted.evidence: DEDR5270 gives Kannada bar and Kodagu bar- come, with Tulu barpini. Belari barɨ preserves the b-r coming stem with final ɨ; no causative is inferred from other formations in the same article. The link is to the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local contact remains subject to review. Upstream cognacy labels are not independent evidence.

DEDR2426 gives Tulu saipini, Kannada sāy and Gadaba say- die. Belari sey fits the s-y death stem, but its e vowel differs from the a/ā/ai comparanda: this remains an explicitly qualified family comparison, not an exact dictionary attestation. The Sanskrit śava comparison in the article does not establish an immediate donor. The link is to the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local contact remains subject to review. Upstream cognacy labels are not independent evidence.

DEDR2023 gives Kannada, Kodagu and Kota kay hand/arm and Tulu kai hand. Belari kay has the same simple k-ay stem and hand sense; the source does not require an additional constituent. The link is to the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local contact remains subject to review. Upstream cognacy labels are not independent evidence.

DEDR4410 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.3) hudari name, alongside Koraga hudari/podari and Tulu pudarů. The source hudarɨ matches this same-language h-d-r name attestation with a different final-vowel transcription; retain ɨ rather than rewriting it as i. The link is to the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local contact remains subject to review. Upstream cognacy labels are not independent evidence.

DEDR4711(a) gives Kannada, Kodagu and Tulu mara tree, alongside Tamil maram. Belari mara matches the complete tree stem, without imposing the Tamil final nasal or transferring the tree-animal compounds in subsection (b). The link is to the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local contact remains subject to review. Upstream cognacy labels are not independent evidence.

DEDR4878 gives Kannada mī/mīyu and Tulu mīpini take a bath, with Parji mī-. Belari mī preserves the long-vowel bathing stem. The source bathe gloss does not imply the causative interpretation of the separately listed mīpāvuni. The proposed link uses the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4758 gives Tulu maḷpuni do/make and Telugu mal(u)cu make/fashion. Belari māḷɨ agrees in the m-retroflex-lateral stem and do sense, but has marked long ā and no -puni. This is a qualified stem-level comparison; the source does not establish a Tulu borrowing route. The proposed link uses the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR5430 explicitly gives Koraga (M.) būḷu and Kodagu būḷ- fall, alongside Tulu būruni. Belari būḷɨ agrees in the long ū and retroflex lateral, differing in the final-vowel transcription; it need not match the Tamil head form. The proposed link uses the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4004 contains the whole ripe-fruit family, including Telugu paṇḍu and Tulu parndů, as well as Kannada paṇ/paṇṇu. Homepage discovery also finds Kannada haṇ/haṇṇu explicitly cited to DEDR4004 in Uchida–Rajapurohit p.904. Belari haṇdɨ combines initial h with a nasal-stop fruit stem; the ṇd and final ɨ are preserved, not normalized to the Kannada form. The Sanskrit phala comparison does not establish a donor. The proposed link uses the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR215 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.2) argi rice. This matches the full source form and sense; it is not Tulu ari with an analyst-inserted stop. The search output mislabels this Belari comparandum as Tulu, corrected here from the full article. The proposed link uses the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4318 gives Kannada por̤e, Kodagu poḷe and Malayalam pur̤a river. Homepage discovery finds Kannada hoḷe stream/small river in Uchida–Rajapurohit p.938, explicitly citing DEDR4318. Belari huḷe is a qualified h-initial lateral-stem comparison, with u versus the Kannada/Kodagu o; it is not an exact primary DEDR attestation. The proposed link uses the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4172 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.3) hugeli shoulder, beside Tulu pugelů/puggelů. Belari hugelɨ matches the same-language h-g-l attestation with final ɨ versus i. Search labels spill the Belari material into Tulu; this proposal follows the full primary article, not that label. The proposed link uses the whole DEDR article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR1 gives Tulu ākuḷu those persons. Belari ākḷɨ remote animate plural agrees in ā-k-lateral with medial vowel reduction and final ɨ. This is the inflected remote pronoun within the whole article, not a proposed lexical compound. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR1 includes Telugu adi that woman or thing, Kodagu adï that thing/those things and widespread ad forms. Belari adɨ is a remote dental-stop demonstrative. Preserve its three separate source records (female singular, inanimate singular and inanimate plural); the article supports shared nonmasculine demonstrative morphology, not three distinct stems. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR5160 gives Tulu ēnů/yēnu I, alongside the yānu series. Belari ēṇɨ preserves long ē and a nasal with final high unrounded vowel; the source retroflex nasal differs from the dictionary Tulu n and remains a qualification, not a transcription repair. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR5154 gives Tulu eṅkuḷů we (exclusive), with Kodagu eŋga we; the full article also includes inclusive uses in other languages. Belari eŋkḷo matches the nasal-velar-lateral plural formation with a reduced medial vowel and final o. The installed inclusive and exclusive records share the same form. Bhat1971 p.123 lists one undifferentiated we form; retain both source records without claiming two independently attested clusivity forms. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4137 explicitly gives Belari (LSB2.3) hijini ant beside Tulu pijinů. The survey hijinɨ matches the full same-language form with final ɨ versus i. This is the specific ant family, not the unrelated hoyda or generic insect search matches. The proposal links to the whole article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4534 gives Kannada poy beat and Kodagu poyy beat, alongside Kota poy- strike with the hand. Homepage discovery also finds Kannada hoyyu beat explicitly citing DEDR4534. Belari hoy matches this h-initial beating stem. Keep it distinct from the unrelated pouring family DEDR4407, despite homonymous hoy search results. The proposal links to the whole article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR3887 explicitly gives Belari (LSB2.3) haṇi say. Belari haṇɨ matches the same-language h-retroflex-nasal stem with final ɨ versus i; the source say gloss is retained, rather than importing the command/send senses of other article members. The proposal links to the whole article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4352 gives Tulu pūjuni smear/rub/daub and the Tamil pūcu family. Belari hūju preserves the long ū and j, with initial h corresponding to Tulu p as described by Bhat1971 pp.120–121. This supports the family comparison but not a uniquely established borrowing route; the Sanskrit comparison in the article is not a donor assertion. The proposal links to the whole article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR636 gives Tulu (B-K.) ubi spit, as well as ubbiyuni and Koraga ubbi. Belari ubi matches the whole simple verb; dictionary variants with gemination or different medial consonants do not require changing its spelling. The proposal links to the whole article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4559 includes Tulu poḷtu time/daylight/sun and Kannada hottu. Belari hoḷtɨ preserves the lateral-stop stem and time sense, with h corresponding to Tulu p and final ɨ versus u. Bhat1971 p.121 compares these time forms; the broader article also contains sun words without requiring a changed survey meaning. The proposal links to the whole article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR1477 gives Tulu kāruni and Kodagu/Kota kār- vomit, alongside Malayalam kāruka. Belari kārɨ preserves the long vowel and rhotic stem with final ɨ. No causative meaning is inferred from the separate causative formations in the article. The proposal links to the whole article; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4715 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.2) marjedi grandchild, with Koraga marje grandson/marji granddaughter and Kolami marge grandchild. Survey marjedɨ matches the complete same-language kinship formation with final ɨ versus i; preserve the gender-neutral grandchild meaning. The whole article includes this formation without requiring it to match the displayed head. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR5415 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.2) burde relative beside Tulu binne kinsman/relative/guest and other hospitality terms. Survey burde relatives matches the complete same-language form; the source plural English gloss does not establish a separate plural suffix or require a banquet gloss. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR1355 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.3) gaḷde field in the paddyfield family, beside Kannada gar̤de/garde/gadde. The full form matches; retain the broader survey field gloss. The questioned Sanskrit mud comparison is not an immediate donor claim. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR583 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.2) ijḍe mortar alongside Tulu ujiḍe/jiḍḍe small mortar. The survey matches the complete Belari form and sense. The article includes both mortars and pestles; its displayed head need not designate the same implement. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR583 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.2) ijgeri pestle alongside Tulu ujjērů/ujverů. Survey ijgerɨ matches the same-language full formation with final ɨ versus i; keep it distinct from ijḍe mortar while linking both to the shared article. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR2677 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.1) simbi carry. Survey simbɨ agrees in the s-mb stem with final ɨ versus i. It is a verb of carrying, not an analyst-derived carrying-pad noun; both occur within the whole family. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR5517 includes the cooking/heat family with Tulu bēyuni/bēpini and Kannada bē, plus Kurux bi’inā and Malto bice/bite. Belari bī cook (something) is a qualified long-ī member of this family; its vowel differs from neighbouring Tulu ē. The article contains transitive cooking as well as intransitive heating, so no unexpressed causative component is supplied. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR2053 gives Tulu (B-K.) koḷu give/grant; several other article members explicitly mean give to a third person. Belari koḷu matches the full form. Bhat1971 p.119 distinguishes its third-person recipient use from itta, retained as a separate unresolved source record; the installed generic give gloss is preserved. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR984 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.1) ogi pull. The full source form matches; other article members express carrying or giving, but those meanings do not replace the Belari pull gloss. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR2747 gives Kannada sey beauty/merit/propriety and saypu rectitude/propriety/merit. Belari seypɨ beautiful is a qualified comparison with this s-y-p formation: the article supplies both the beauty sense and the -p formation, although not the exact Belari adjective. Preserve e and final ɨ; the whole article, not just its displayed head, is proposed. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR5488 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.2) bergi back, beside Tulu beri and Kannada ben/bennu. Survey bergi matches the complete Belari form and body-part sense; no need to invent a derivation from the similarly related spatial expressions in the article. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4460(a) explicitly records Belari (LSB2.2) hodkuḷu navel. The full form, including the medial dk sequence, exactly matches the survey. Preserve it rather than normalizing to Kannada hokkuḷu or requiring the head form to display this sequence. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR3422 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.2) teru way, alongside Tamil teru street/highway/public road and Telugu teruvu way/road/path. Survey teru path or road matches the complete Belari form and compatible meaning. The questioned Kota comparison does not qualify the separately listed Belari attestation. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR5528 gives Kodagu bōḍ- beg and Tulu bēḍuni beg, with bōḍu want. Belari bōḍɨ agrees with the Kodagu long-ō retroflex-stop begging stem, retaining final ɨ. The whole article includes this rounded-vowel branch; it need not match the Tamil head vowel. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR3888 gives Tamil paṇi bow/be lowered and Kannada (Hal.) hənuku bend/bow. Homepage discovery additionally finds Kannada haṇi bow/bend explicitly citing3888. Belari haṇi bend is a qualified h-initial nasal-stem comparison. Keep it separate from the distinct Belari haṇɨ say record under3887; similar spellings do not merge the meanings. DEDR516 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.1) ija climb down. Survey ija go down (descend) matches the full form and direction of movement; no causative or load-lowering sense is supplied. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR710 records Koraga (M.) ujji keep, not Belari: the full prose corrects the loose search language label. Belari ujji is an exact form-and-sense comparison with that neighbouring-language attestation within the be/stay/keep family. It is not claimed as an explicit Belari DEDR citation. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR3783 explicitly records Belari (LSB2.1) noḍi wash, with Tulu neḍi/niḍiyuni and Parji noḍ-. Survey noḍi matches the complete Belari form; keep it distinct from unrelated noḍi speech and nōḍ- seeing words. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR557(a) includes Tamil utu and Kannada udu demonstratives, and explicitly treats Tulu undu this thing as a nearer demonstrative. Belari uttu is a qualified u-plus-dental demonstrative comparison, with geminate tt versus t/d/nd. Preserve its three separate proximal records (female singular, inanimate singular and plural). The full family includes proximal uses, so the article’s intermediate-distance head description does not exclude these forms. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR4205 gives Kannada peṟagu backside/behind/afterwards and Tamil piṟaku back, alongside Tulu piravu behind. Belari haragɨ is a qualified h-r-g comparison: initial h accords with the p:h correspondence noted for Belari, but a versus e/i and final ɨ versus u remain explicit differences. Link to the whole behind family, not by the displayed head alone. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR5151 includes Telugu endu where, Kannada etta where and entu how, with a broad e-interrogative formation family. Belari entɨ where is a qualified e-n-dental comparison, retaining its voiceless t and final ɨ rather than rewriting it as endu. The source place interrogative is preserved; the article groups these related functions without requiring identical forms. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR2495 gives Malayalam cikkiṇi young/small, Kannada ciga little/small and Tulu cikini tender/young/small. Belari sigɨṇi a little is a qualified s-g-nasal formation comparison: retain voiced g, medial ɨ and retroflex ṇ rather than normalize to any one comparandum. DEDR1603 has kinni/kinkana but lacks the initial s/c series, making2495 the better candidate. The Sanskrit/Prakrit comparisons do not establish a donor. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

DEDR1148 gives Kannada/Tulu gaṭṭi hard/firm and explicitly Gondi (Ko.) gaṭṭi very, so the whole article includes an intensifying use. Belari gaṭṭiya much is a qualified extension of this gaṭṭi formation with final -ya, whose precise morphology remains unresolved. Preserve the source quantity gloss; the proposal is not justified solely by the hard/firm head. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.

Bhat (1971), printed p.119 (PDF p.126), gives iḷa get up; the installed wake up gloss is compatible with DEDR851(a), whose Kannada er̤/ēr̤u includes rise and awake and Kodagu ë·ḷ- means get up. Bhat p.121 independently describes Belari ḷ corresponding to Proto-Dravidian ẓ. This is a qualified whole-family comparison: Belari high short i versus the quoted mid/long vowels remains unexplained, and no particular borrowing route is established.

held.reason: DEDR586 has Kannada oḍal and Tulu uḍalů/oḍālů belly, a plausible medial-stem match. Belari initial h is not present in the full article comparanda; preserve the source form and seek a direct Belari attestation or evidence for this prothesis before proposing the link.

DEDR741 (ūtu/ūdu/ūbu) and DEDR751 (ūr-/urpu) both contain mouth-blowing verbs. Belari ū lacks the consonants distinguishing them. Full articles read; retain both candidates until a paradigm or direct comparative source establishes which family explains this short form.

Tulu boy comparanda āṇů and paiyerů do not explain baggerɨ. Form search finds unrelated intention/bending/where words. No supported child-family assignment from these results; shared material with beggi girl needs independent evidence.

Form search finds Kannada fear verbs, while Tulu girl terms have different stems. No evidence yet derives Belari beggi from those words or explains it alongside baggerɨ boy. Preserve as a complete unresolved form.

DEDR4694 includes Kannada madive/maduve and Tulu madůmè marriage. Belari madiyeri has unexplained -yeri relative to these comparanda. Full article read; do not reduce the complete source formation to an assumed mad- stem or fabricate a component link.

Tulu tāyi and other mother terms in DEDR364 do not explain tanne geminate n and short vowel. Form search finds unrelated cold/reflexive matches; those do not establish mother ancestry. Need a direct comparandum or a justified kinship formation.

Full DEDR3999 gives Tulu paḷi/pardi elder sister and Koraga hareddi/pareḍi, but the kinship sequence is introduced with a question mark. Bhat compares Belari haḷdi to Tulu paldi under p:h. This is a good local comparison; its placement in the old/aged article remains qualified by the dictionary itself. Hold pending resolution of that article-level uncertainty, not because the head must match.

Tulu son-in-law search points to marmāye and aḷiya. Full DEDR4715 does not explain Belari himbaḍɨ; 2410 is only a search lead, not a verified analysis. No reliable whole-form kinship route established.

Tulu wife search yields boḍedi and unrelated kinship terms; form search returns treading, fenugreek, chief and plough words with different senses or consonants. No supported whole-form wife etymology established; do not force a resemblance link.

DEDR5485 has Tulu bedůrů and Kannada bidiru/bidaru bamboo. Belari debirɨ may invite a b-d metathesis analysis, but this is not established by the full article or the current source evidence. Preserve as a candidate, not a confirmed link.

Tulu forest discovery supplies kāna/kāḍů/pāḍi/malɛ; relaxed hula search yields other tree names and unrelated words, not a supported whole-form forest match. Do not turn a generic forest gloss into a particular tree or field interpretation without evidence.

DEDR1204 supplies katti/katte knife across southern languages but does not explain final -ge in Belari kattige. Exact relaxed form discovery only finds unrelated comb material. Full article read; retain complete source form pending morphological evidence.

Medicine family DEDR4719 has Tulu mardů and Kannada mardu/maddu, but Belari maḷgɨ has an unexplained lateral-velar cluster. Form search finds unrelated lying/decreasing/cloud words. No justified correspondence or whole-form medicine analysis yet.

Tulu pig search supplies pañji and unrelated compound hits; relaxed sāgo search supplies cultivation/plant material. No supported whole-form pig cognate or borrowing route yet. No inference of absence beyond these queries.

DEDR3122 has Kui tāṛa/tāṛi- dig and other scratching/digging forms, but Belari tari differs in marked vowel quantity and rhotic articulation. No close southern or same-language attestation found by current searches; retain this as a candidate needing correspondence evidence.

Full DEDR4321 gives Koraga boḷa float and Tulu pulāvuni, a plausible family lead, but Belari baḷi differs in both vowels. DEDR3464 tēl- is semantically apt but less close in consonants. Keep the source form unresolved pending stronger comparison.

Bhat1971 p.119 describes giving to first/second person, contrasting koḷu. Form search has not established an article explaining the complete itta stem. Recipient semantics alone cannot force it under the tar- give family or turn it into a variant of koḷu.

Relaxed form search returns shining and departing families, not rubbing. Tulu rubbing verbs have different full forms. Do not link to a phonetic match with an unrelated meaning or discard the Belari ending.

Tulu wearing search supplies tuttuni and DEDR3319 contains tutt-/tūnd-/tund- formations. None directly explains Belari uḷu. Relaxed form search only matches unrelated words or English swear; no supported full-form wearing analysis yet.

Original Bhat (1971) printed p.120 (PDF p.127) visually confirms the spelling and gloss chilly among household/food nouns; this is not an OCR substitution. DEDR4867 offers a strong pepper/chilli family lead: Kannada mor̤asu/mer̤asu, Malayalam muḷaku, Kota meḷg and Kodagu maḷu. Interpreting chilly as the food noun would conflict with the installed cold gloss. Retain the record unchanged and hold the link for explicit semantic adjudication; vowel and consonant details also need qualification.

Tulu good search offers eḍḍe, sajji, nala and others; relaxed gant search has not established a matching good adjective. Full gantadɨ, including final -adɨ, remains unexplained. No unsupported segmentation or donor claim.

DEDR3821 gives Tulu paji and wider pacc-/pas- green forms. Initial p:h is supported in Belari, but the survey retroflex ḍ versus Tulu j still needs an attested correspondence or verified source reading. Preserve haḍi; do not silently rewrite it haji.

Tulu rough gloss search and relaxed dabra form search have not established a supported full-form comparison. Retain as unresolved; possible loans require evidence for an immediate donor rather than a guessed distant root.

DEDR1670 has kuṇṭe/kuṇṭu short/dwarf while DEDR1851 has Tulu kundri little/small/short. The Belari ṇṭr sequence does not choose cleanly between these families. Full articles read; retain both and resolve morphology/correspondences before assignment.

Relaxed form discovery returns son-in-law, responsibility, and small-pond entries whose modifiers are not evidence for the Belari adjective small. Neither the long vowel nor the complete form has a supported small-family comparison yet.

DEDR3268(a) supplies Kannada sī/sīyi/sihi and Tulu śī sweet, but Belari sīge has an unexplained -ge. Full article, including honey subsection, read; do not infer a component or donor from the short shared initial alone.

Tulu blood discovery supplies netterů, but full DEDR3748 has no comparandum explaining Belari oḍivu. Relaxed form search returns unrelated words. This is an unresolved blood term; do not force the dominant local blood family onto it.

DEDR2286 supplies Kannada jaṅge and Telugu jaṅga stride, and explicitly says the listed words probably derive from Sanskrit jaṅghā lower leg. Belari jaŋgɨ foot or leg is suggestive but lacks a verified immediate donor route. Do not attach as inherited merely because the stride forms share this article; do not bypass the donor with a Sanskrit ancestry link.

DEDR1253 includes Tulu kekki/kekkilů and Koraga gekkili neck. Belari gōke differs in vowel quantity and quality and consonant length; the source evidence has not established those correspondences. Exact relaxed form discovery found no matching dictionary form. Keep as an open candidate.

DEDR5515 has veṟṟ-ilai and a questioned Tulu baccirè comparison competing with3821. Belari bātre is not directly explained by those forms; no full-form match from current search. Retain leaf gloss and do not create an unattested compound or donor.
Tulu bridge search supplies only an unrelated supporting-pole expression; relaxed sāro search yields no matching article. Need a primary whole-form bridge comparison or documented borrowing route.
Tulu drum names do not explain kaḍvayi; the closest form-search hit is kadvāya cheek, a different meaning. No justified metaphor or compound analysis connects that hit to this drum word.
Tulu firewood query gives unrelated fuel terms; relaxed seyle query finds no matching article. No supported whole-form firewood analysis yet; search absence is limited to these queries.

DEDR946 supplies Tulu oṭṭe hole and wider breaking/hole formations, but Belari oṭre has an unexplained rhotic. Other form matches are unrelated verbs or poṭre tree hollow. Preserve the entire hole form pending sound or morphological evidence.

Tulu lid search supplies mucc- formations; relaxed aḍāk search has not explained complete aḍākina lid. Possible verbal formation requires independent morphological analysis, not an invented component division.

Homepage Kannada hakkalu includes waste land without trees, but full DEDR4423 gives only questioned hakkalu gleanings within pick/gather. Belari plain cannot be assigned there solely from the search-added land sense. Need evidence linking the senses and resolving the dictionary uncertainty.

Tulu climbing forms and relaxed uppar search do not establish the complete Belari upparsɨ climb. The superficially similar uppēruni in710 is cattle copulating with an explicit climb constituent, not evidence for this full form. Morphological analysis remains open.
Tulu throw query supplies unrelated aḍak-, udēv-, pāḍ- and bī- formations; socco form search has no match. No supported whole-form or component analysis yet.

Blighted search gives the unrelated poṭṭu/poṭi family4491, whose full article does not explain saṭrɨ. Relaxed saṭr search yields no match. Source blighted meaning remains unchanged; do not attach based only on gloss.

Slough search finds skin/peeling family652 (uri) and skin-cover family3981 (pare; newer Kannada entries add hore/hare). Belari huri could invite either initial-h prothesis or vowel correspondence, neither established here. Full articles read. Retain competing candidates rather than choosing by spelling alone.

DEDR2313 gives Kannada daṇḍe vicinity/adjoining and Telugu daṇḍa side/proximity, but no explicit coast sense. Broader Kannada bank discovery has not resolved that semantic development. Full article read; preserve coast pending direct evidence, not an automatic side-to-shore inference.
